name: LEAPS Protective Put (portfolio hedge)
summary: Buy long-dated index-ETF puts (SPY/QQQ) sized to the whole portfolio's beta-weighted delta, as standing crash insurance.

legs.strike_rule: Delta -0.15 to -0.25 on SPY or QQQ; quantity = beta-weighted portfolio delta / 100, rounded down

max_profit: (strike - index level) x 100 x contracts - debit; large in a crash
max_loss: Total debit. Expect this to be a persistent cost in any up market - it is insurance, and insurance is supposed to lose money most of the time.
breakevens: strike - debit per share on the index

greeks.delta: -0.15 to -0.25 per contract against a positive portfolio delta
greeks.gamma: positive, grows sharply in a selloff
greeks.theta: negative but small per day at this duration
greeks.vega: large positive - the main source of P&L in a fast selloff, often before delta even matters

when_to_use: When the portfolio's beta-weighted delta exceeds a risk threshold and VIX is low (VIX < 16, when tail hedges are cheapest).
entry_rules: Only buy when VIX < 18; hedges bought during a spike are a wealth transfer
Compute beta-weighted portfolio delta against SPY; hedge 40-70% of it, never 100%
Annual hedge budget capped at 1.5% of equity (~$750/yr on $50k)
SPY or QQQ only - index-ETF options are penny-wide and deeply liquid
management_rules: Roll annually when DTE < 180, into the same delta 270+ days out
Monetisation rule: if the put's value reaches 3x the debit, sell 50% and roll the remainder down to a fresh -0.20 delta strike. This converts a paper crash gain into cash without abandoning the hedge
Re-size the hedge quarterly as portfolio delta changes
Never increase the hedge during a selloff - that is buying vega at the peak
exit_rules: Roll at DTE < 180; monetise 50% at 3x; fully exit only if the underlying portfolio is liquidated
Never carry to expiry: auto-exercise would create a short index-ETF position
assignment_risk: None (long). Auto-exercise into short SPY shares is the hazard, prevented by the 180-DTE roll rule.
liquidity_needs: SPY/QQQ LEAPS puts - among the most liquid long-dated contracts available.
common_mistakes: Buying the hedge after the crash starts; hedging 100% of delta and guaranteeing underperformance; never monetising a winning hedge.
